The labs show a cholestatic pattern with significantly elevated Alkaline Phosphatase and direct hyperbilirubinemia, which strongly supports a biliary obstruction or disease. Given your history of ulcerative colitis, this presentation is classic for Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.

The cholestatic pattern with severe pruritus in a patient with ulcerative colitis is highly suggestive of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, even though the MRCP was reported as normal, which can occur in early or small-duct disease. Given the exclusion of other common causes like PBC and viral hepatitis, I will proceed with this diagnosis.
